risk_if_not_implemented: Without Cyber Incident Reporting for Sensitive / Regulated Data, security incidents may not be detected, contained, investigated or communicated in a timely manner, increasing their scope, duration and cost. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), Delayed Containment / Increased Incident Impact (R-IR-2), Privacy Harm / Unauthorized Processing (R-IP-6), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11).

compensating_control_1.name: Contacts With Authorities
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and document appropriate contacts with relevant law enforcement and regulatory bodies.
compensating_control_1.justification: Contacts With Authorities (GOV-15) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Cyber Incident Reporting for Sensitive / Regulated Data (IRO-16.2) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Incident Stakeholder Reporting
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to timely-report incidents to applicable:
(1) Internal stakeholders; 
(2) Affected clients & third-parties; and
(3) Regulatory authorities.
compensating_control_2.justification: Incident Stakeholder Reporting (IRO-16) provides incident response capability that compensates for the absence of Cyber Incident Reporting for Sensitive / Regulated Data (IRO-16.2) by enabling timely detection, containment, and recovery from security events in the absence of the primary control. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
